title: Lip-strengthening exercise and the mouthpiece cork
summary: Henry demonstrates strengthening his lips with the slide and a vacuum, then shows how he fits a cork in a valve.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Well, you were telling about that system once, developing your lips the way you practiced with the... Well, I get much of the scouting. Oh, sure. All right. I'll stop it. Well, you have just your slide there.
Just use the slide. You see? You put your thumb in.
On the end of the slide.
See how I pulled your lips?

Yeah. And you just work the slide up and down as if you're playing. But you keep that sort of like pumping, sucking pressure there on your lip. Take the bell off and put your thumb over there and make a vacuum ring. And you figure that strengthens... It does. It pulls the muscles in your lips. Pulls the muscles there.

It makes them super. Because my partner, he said that was our monk. But I have a warner. You see, the man that showed me was a professional trombone player. Sometimes your lips don't vibrate properly.
Sure.
And if you wake them, get them super in the morning...
You work on that a little bit each?
Just before you get ready to go play.
Just before you play. You still like to warm up.
You warm your lips up. See, you get your muscles pulled up. And then after you get your muscles pulled up, well then you don't have no trouble. Your lips vibrate properly. You put that in yourself.
I put that in myself. Using a great big cart there so it can't leak around.
It don't leak. See how that fits in there?
Oh yeah. That's a nice job. I'm not going to have to do that with my cornet.
I just take some of that paste glue and put it on here and stick it in there.
And press it down.
Press it down. Now when this wears out from the water, I just take and cut another cork. Yeah. Just like you get one of these corks out of a whiskey bottle.
Yeah, about three quarters or two thirds of an inch.
Well, you can use any pint cork or half pint cork and you cut it to suit the valve, you know. Yeah.
